CHIEF COMPLAINT
Nonhealing foot ulcer with recent drainage and redness.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with a nonhealing foot ulcer on the right foot that has been present for approximately two months. Patient reports that the ulcer recently became red and started draining, which prompted concern. Patient recalls obtaining the injury from walking barefoot at Dewey Beach. The wound sometimes throbs but patient denies specific localized pain. Patient was seen by PCP prior to this visit and was prescribed antibiotics, though patient has not yet filled the prescription and cannot recall the specific medication name, though reports having taken it before.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports occasional throbbing sensation in the foot but denies specific pain. Patient reports recent onset of drainage and redness from the wound. Vital signs are normal and patient denies fever.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus.

MEDICATIONS
Patient reports taking diabetes medication but does not check blood sugar regularly. Specific diabetes medications not detailed. Patient was prescribed antibiotics by PCP but has not filled prescription.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as an ambulance driver. Patient reports walking barefoot at Dewey Beach where injury occurred.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, no fever. Right foot exam reveals a one by two inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, just proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. Wound shows redness, drainage, and surrounding edema. No necrosis, odor, or bony exposure noted. Patient reports increased pressure sensation but no distinct pain with palpation.

RESULTS
Right foot X-ray: No evidence of osteomyelitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diabetic foot ulcer with infection. Plan includes: (1) Order ankle-brachial index to assess blood supply to foot; (2) Perform debridement to remove dead tissue; (3) Prescribe clindamycin 400 mg twice daily for seven days to treat infection; (4) Provide surgical shoe to reduce pressure on wound for next month; (5) Follow-up appointment in two weeks with possible repeat debridement. Patient instructed to call office with any concerns and to seek urgent care or emergency department if fever develops or if condition worsens.
